'''Onkar Nath Srivastava''' (31 December 1942 – 24 April 2021)<ref name="TNN 2021" /> was an Indian material physicist, an [[Emeritus professor]] of [[Banaras Hindu University]] and the vice president for India and South Asia of the International Association for Hydrogen Energy, who was known for his contributions to the disciplines of [[nanotechnology]] and hydrogen energy.<ref name="Board of Directors">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iahe.org/boardofdirectors.asp |title=Board of Directors |date=2016 |access-date=9 August 2016 |website=Board of Directors |publisher=International Association for Hydrogen Energy |archive-date=27 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160627092731/http://www.iahe.org/boardofdirectors.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the author of two books and over 440 scientific papers<ref name="O. N. Srivastava on Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user |title=O. N. Srivastava on Google Scholar |date=2016 |access-date=9 August 2016 |website=O. N. Srivastava |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref> and a recipient of several honors including [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], the highest Indian award in the science and technology categories.<ref name="VermaSrivastava1991">{{cite book|author1=A. R. Verma|author2=O. N. Srivastava|title=Crystallography Applied to Solid State Physics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=usDm2mOOZQAC&pg=PA466|year=1991|publisher=New Age International|isbn=978-81-224-0321-3|pages=466–}}</ref> The Government of India awarded him the fourth highest civilian honour of the [[Padma Shri]], in 2016, for his contributions to science and engineering.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/PadmaAwards_25012016.pdf |title=Padma Awards |date=2016 |access-date=9 August 2016 |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170803085913/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/PadmaAwards_25012016.pdf |archive-date=3 August 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Srivastava was born on 31 December 1942, in [[Varanasi]], the holy city of Lord Shiva in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]].<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |access-date=9 August 2016 |website=Brief Profile of the Awardee |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> He secured his master's degree in Physics (MSc) in 1961 from [[Banaras Hindu University]] (BHU) and followed it up with a doctoral degree (PhD) from the same institution, under the guidance of renowned physicist [[Ajit Ram Verma]], in 1966.<ref name="Indian Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N94-1166 |title=Indian Fellow |date=2016 |access-date=9 August 2016 |website=Indian Fellow |publisher=Indian National Science Academy}}</ref> After doing his post doctoral research at [[Cornell University]], USA, he returned to India to start his career as a lecturer at Banaras Hindu University where he served in different capacities as that of a reader, professor, head of the department of physics and the coordinator of the ''Centre of Advance Studies-Hydrogen Energy Centre''. After his superannuation from service, he continues his association with the university as a professor emeritus<ref name="BHU eyes hydrogen as fuel for future">{{Cite news |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/BHU-eyes-hydrogen-as-fuel-for-future/articleshow/16536919.cms |title=BHU eyes hydrogen as fuel for future |last=Swati Chandra |date=25 September 2012 |access-date=9 August 2016 |newspaper=Times of India}}</ref> and as an associate faculty member of ''Condensed Matter Experiment'' research program of the university.<ref name="Condensed Matter Experiment">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/physics/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040708063636/http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/physics/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 July 2004 |title=Condensed Matter Experiment |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |website=Present Research Programs |publisher=Banaras Hindu University}}</ref>

Srivastava, a former member of the board of directors of [[The World Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="Biography of Onkar N. Srivastava">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iahe.org/boardofdirectors.asp?did=18 |title=Biography of Onkar N. Srivastava |date=2016 |access-date=9 August 2016 |website=Vice President for India and South Asia, IAHE |publisher=International Association for Hydrogen Energy |archive-date=28 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428180327/http://iahe.org/boardofdirectors.asp?did=18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was the vice president (India & South Asia) of the International Association of Hydrogen Energy, having been elected to the position in 2012, where he also serves as a member of their editorial board.<ref name="Board of Directors" /> Under his guidance, the Hydrogen Energy Centre of BHU was involved in advance research on the practical applications of hydrogen fuel, in association with the [[Ministry of New and Renewable Energy]] and the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] (DST), of the Government of India.<ref name="BHU eyes hydrogen as fuel for future" /> He published two books, ''Crystallography Applied to Solid State Physics''<ref name="VermaSrivastava1991" /> and ''Formation and phase stability of Al based quasicrystals: Quasicrystal''<ref name="Formation and phase stability of Al based quasicrystals: Quasicrystal">{{Cite book |title=Formation and phase stability of Al based quasicrystals: Quasicrystal |last=Thakur Prasad Yadav, Onkar Nath Srivastava |publisher=LAP LAMBERT Academic Publishing |year=2012 |isbn=978-3847320883 |pages=216 }}</ref> and over 440 scientific papers.<ref name="Onkar Nath Srivastava on Microsoft Academic Search">{{Cite web |url=http://65.54.113.26/Author/13375348/onkar-nath-srivastava |title=Onkar Nath Srivastava on Microsoft Academic Search |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |website=Academic / Authors |publisher=Microsoft Academic Search }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="O. N. Srivastava on PubFacts">{{Cite web |url=http://www.pubfacts.com/author/Onkar+Nath+Srivastava |title=O. N. Srivastava on PubFacts |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |website=Publications Authored by O. N. Srivastava |publisher=PubFacts}}</ref> He delivered keynote addresses in a number of science seminars and undertook several projects for various government agencies; ''Nanoscience and Technology'' of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] (2005–2010), ''Support to Hydrogen Energy Centre'' (2007–2012), ''Development & Demonstration of Hydrogen Catalytic Combustion Cookers'' (2007–2010), ''Development & Demonstration of Hydrogen Fueled three wheelers'' (2009–2012), ''Mission Mode Project on Hydrogen Storage Materials (Hydride)'' (2009–2014), all of the [[Ministry of New and Renewable Energy]], and ''Synthesis Characterization and Properties of Single Walled Carbon Nanotubes'' (2009–2012) of the [[Defence Research and Development Organization]] are some of the notable ones.<ref name="Dr. O.N. Srivastava on BHU">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/physics/onsrivastava.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211051901/http://www.bhu.ac.in/science/physics/onsrivastava.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 December 2013 |title=Dr. O.N. Srivastava on BHU |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |publisher=Banaras Hindu University}}</ref> He was also involved in organizing science conferences<ref name="Organizing Committee">{{Cite web |url=http://nanotechbhu.com/venue.html |title=Organizing Committee |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |website=Nanotechnology |publisher=Banaras Hindu University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170226182614/http://nanotechbhu.com/venue.html |archive-date=26 February 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and mentored 87 doctoral students.<ref name="Board of Directors" />

Srivastava died from [[COVID-19]] in April 2021.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/padma-awardee-bhu-prof-nano-physicist-dies-of-covid/articleshow/82248388.cms | title=Padma awardee BHU prof & nano physicist dies of Covid &#124; Varanasi News - Times of India | website=[[The Times of India]] | date=26 April 2021 }}</ref>

In 1988, The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR) awarded Srivastava the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], the highest Indian science award for his contributions on ''high temperature oxide superconductors, growth, characterization and application of hydrogen storage materials''.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee" /> He received the Goyal Prize in Physical Sciences and K. S. Rao Memorial Award on Renewable Energy in 2000 and two years later, the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] awarded him the 2002 Homi J. Bhabha Award in Applied Sciences.<ref name="Dr. O.N. Srivastava on BHU" /> In 2009, he was recognized by the ICSC with the Material Research Society of India-ICSC Award.<ref name="Biography of Onkar N. Srivastava" /> The [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] elected him as their fellow in 1989,<ref name="NASI Fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |title=NASI Fellows |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |publisher=The National Academy of Sciences, India |archive-date=16 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316043224/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |url-status=dead }}</ref> followed by the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 1994<ref name="Indian Fellow" /> and the International Association of Hydrogen Energy in 2010.<ref name="Onkar N. Srivastava (India)">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iahe.org/fellow.asp |title=Onkar N. Srivastava (India) |date=2016 |access-date=10 August 2016 |website=IAHE fellows |publisher=International Association for Hydrogen Energy |archive-date=28 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228014649/http://iahe.org/fellow.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also an elected fellow of the Asia Pacific Academy of Materials, International Academy of Physical Sciences and the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Dr. O.N. Srivastava on BHU" />
